separators\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022The pull request footer line (run id and token count) is updated on every follow-up push, not written once at PR-open: it names the current run of record and the CUMULATIVE token total across every run that carried the pull request (origin example, 2026-08-21: PR 21\\u0027s footer still named the original run and 18_401_309 tokens while twelve later generations had multiplied the real figure)\u0022,\u0022h9k task show gains a tokens surface: one line per run (generation, run id short form, input/output tokens) and a task total, reading from the TokensRecorded events / RunDetails projection that already exist - display composition, no new capture\u0022,\u0022Every token count rendered anywhere (PR footer, task show, any future status surface) goes through one shared formatter using underscore group separators (18_401_309), culture-invariant\u0022,\u0022The closeout monitor\\u0027s existing follow-up push seam is where the footer update rides - no new polling, no extra GitHub calls beyond the edit itself; a failed footer edit never fails the push or the run\u0022,\u0022dotnet build and dotnet test pass\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Feature\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Brian\\u0027s ask (2026-08-21, orchestrator session): are we updating the token number in\\nthe PR description as we go (no - written once at open, stale by generation 4), how\\ndo I see it for a task in h9k (you cannot yet - the events exist, no display reads\\nthem), and format the numbers with underscores rather than commas.\\n\\nDesign constraints:\\n- DRAFT ONLY at creation - Brian refines this alongside the backlog documents\\n  before publishing.\\n- Collides with PR 21\\u0027s files (PullRequestBody/PullRequestOpener, TaskShowCommand);\\n  queue only after task 17 reaches true closeout.\\n- Cumulative means every session the platform recorded for the task\\u0027s runs: build\\n  sessions, review cycles, fix runs, follow-ups. retrying or resolving a failed dependency clears the dead-blocker hold instead of leaving the board crying wolf\u0022,\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:[\u0022When a Failed blocker is retried (TaskRetried) or resolved (TaskResolved), its dependents\\u0027 recorded dependency-failure is cleared by a recovery event on each dependent (e.g. TaskDependencyRecovered naming the blocker), returning them to plain Blocked with the ordinary waiting-on display\u0022,\u0022The same clearing applies when the dependency set is revised to drop the dead blocker (the already-taught remedy keeps working)\u0022,\u0022The resolver never re-records a failure for a blocker that is currently Queued, Claimed, or otherwise capable of reaching closeout again; dead-blocker holds are for blockers that are dead NOW\u0022,\u0022h9k status stops showing NeedsHuman for a dependent whose blockers are all either healthy or complete; the recovery is visible within one dispatch-loop cycle of the blocker\\u0027s retry\u0022,\u0022History stays honest: the original DependencyFailed record and the recovery both remain on the stream - the hold happened, and so did the recovery\u0022,\u0022dotnet build and dotnet test pass\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Bugfix\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Origin incident (2026-08-21): the platform\\u0027s first overnight crash-recovery ran\\nthrough the first real dependency graph. The machine went down with the chain\\u0027s\\nhead running; on daemon start the orphan was failed honestly and both dependents\\nwere held-for-human with the dead-blocker reason - all correct. Then h9k task\\nretry put the blocker back to work, and the holds did not clear: both dependents\\nkept reading NeedsHuman for what would have been the whole rebuild, hours of a\\nboard saying \\u0022act now\\u0022 about a situation already handled. The unblock-at-closeout\\npath ignores the stale record, so this is display honesty rather than a\\ncorrectness bug - but a status surface that overstates urgency trains its reader\\nto ignore it.\\n\\nDesign constraints:\\n- The recovery event is appended by the same resolver pass that records failures\\n  (one owner for dependency state transitions), driven by observing the blocker\\u0027s\\n  actual state - never by assuming the retry will succeed.\\n- A blocker that is retried and fails AGAIN re-records the failure; MaxConcurrentRuns (default 3): the dispatch sweep claims a queued task only while the node\\u0027s count of live runs is below the ceiling; everything else stays Queued - which already honestly means waiting - and is claimed as slots free up, oldest assignment first\u0022,\u0022The count of live runs means agent sessions the daemon is supervising right now: build sessions, review cycles, fix runs, follow-ups, synthesis passes all occupy the slot of the run that owns them; a run releases its slot when its session tree is done (completed, failed, parked, or following-up with no live session), not at true closeout - a task waiting on a merge observation holds no memory\u0022,\u0022h9k status shows the pressure honestly when the ceiling is the reason nothing dispatches: a queued row that is waiting for a slot says so in one line (per the backlog-28 reason discipline), so a quiet board reads as throttled, not stalled\u0022,\u0022The daemon log states the ceiling at startup and logs each deferred claim once (task id, current live count), never per-sweep spam\u0022,\u0022The ceiling is configuration, not code: DaemonOptions like the review caps, so the Windows tower and the Mac laptop can carry different numbers per their memory\u0022,\u0022dotnet build and dotnet test pass\u0022],\u0022Type\u0022:\u0022Feature\u0022,\u0022AgentContext\u0022:\u0022Origin incident (2026-08-21, twice The dispatch engine claims everything eligible with no\\nceiling - the machine, not the platform, ends up enforcing one, by killing agents.\\n\\nDesign constraints:\\n- Queued-waiting-for-slot is NOT a new task state: the task is Queued, the reason\\n  line is display composition from the daemon\\u0027s live-run count (backlog-28 shape).\\n- Composes with backlog 29 (slim agent profile): 29 they\\n  belong to a run that already holds one, and counting them separately would let\\n  two builds plus their reviews exceed the ceiling the number was chosen to protect.\\n- Sequencing: touches
